target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model'\''s custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) when the config'\''s `models` map was created with an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy the legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, so an inherited key matching `converted` was treated as an existing own entry. The migration then skipped the copy and deleted the original `claude-cli/*` key, losing the user'\''s model configuration.

Switching to `Object.hasOwn(next, converted)` makes the check operate on own properties only, matching the fix in #103373 for the Anthropic default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users with prototype-bearing or otherwise inherited `models` maps no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata when migrating to Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that constructs a `models` object with an inherited `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` key and verifies the migrated `claude-cli/claude-opus-4-7` entry is written as an own property.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts` passes (16/16).
- `pnpm oxfmt` and `pnpm oxlint` pass on the changed files.

Related: #103373
